item.title: Re: I Am Requesting A Greenlight On A Concept
item.content:encoded:
Hello Dr Camero! lets take a look :)

SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A katana, longbow, and samurai armor, with anomalous properties, crafted using an unknown element.

What are the anomalous properties? what does the skip do? does it have a purpose? what is this 'unknown element'?-what part does this have in the narrative? what about this will make me as the reader care?

-Currently the skip doesn't really show anything outwardly interesting or unique, as it doesn't have much going for it other than the effects (which themselves are quite vague). As a result, the skip comes across as a bit cliched and dime a dozen, as there are already a fair few amount of sword and weaponry related articles on the main-site, and this concept (in its current state) doesn't seem to bring anything new to the table. Which in turn, makes it hard for me get invested in the idea, or confident that it would work in its current state.

The narrative:

Central Narrative: A katana that is forged from an unknown smith, a longbow with arrows that will seek the wielders target, and armor that is practically unbreakable.

This is closer to additional info than a story, there isn't any sort of setup, middle act, payoff or conflict shown here. How will the current idea fit into a narrative?- what would the article look like? What direction will the story take? are there any characters? how does the Foundation get involved? whats the main conflict? whats everything building up to? what will make me as the reader invested in this?

I would highly recommend starting development on a narrative, as they can help with audience engagement and can further explain the skip. Modern audiences tend to favour skips with a narrative, which has lead to them more or less becoming the standard. The narrative doesn't need to be a long winded saga, short stories can work very well if done right.

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The sword can drain exact amounts of blood, and heal wounds perfectly once the blood is lost. The longbow can shoot arrows at unnatural speeds and the arrows can always hit their mark. The armor is from a time period that didn't exist when it was made, and can't be destroyed.

This isn't really much of a hook, it's more or less a bunch or specific effects which alone don't keep my interest as there isn't much behind them. What part does this play in the story? whats their purpose?

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight

If you would like me review this (or any concept) further, then please feel free to send me a PM or ask via IRC. Response times generally range from 2-12 hours over PMs. If your looking for additional critiques in general, then I would highly recommend contacting the butterfly squad :)

Cheers,

-RED
